title: Constant-time tag comparison in an HLS MAC verifier
submission_contract: Participants harden inputs/mac_verify.cpp (and, if strictly necessary, inputs/mac_verify.h without changing the pinned signature) in place. The evaluator compiles these files with g++ against a private test harness and grades behaviorally.
pinned_interface: bool verify(const unsigned char computed_tag[16], const unsigned char received_tag[16]);

metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of targeted security requirements for which behavioral analysis flags observable data-dependent timing/branching in the compiled verify(); lower is better.

metrics.name: information_flow_correctness
metrics.description: Measured invariance of verification latency/instruction count across mismatch-position buckets relative to a calibrated non-constant-time reference, expressed as a normalized score (1.0 = fully invariant, 0.0 = as position-dependent as the naive reference).

metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of functional/compile requirements (FR1-FR4) that pass when compiling and running mac_verify.cpp against the evaluation harness with g++.

expected_output_summary: A correctly hardened mac_verify.cpp compiles cleanly with g++ against mac_verify.h and the evaluator's harness, and the resulting verify() function returns true only when all 16 bytes of computed_tag and received_tag match exactly and false otherwise across known-answer vectors, single-byte-mismatch vectors at every position, multi-byte-mismatch vectors, and the all-zero and all-0xFF edge cases. In addition, repeated timed invocations of verify() across mismatch-position buckets (early, middle, late first-differing byte, and full match) show statistically invariant latency/operation counts, with no systematic trend tied to where the first mismatch occurs.
